extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings (attorneys/agents before the USPTO), OED staff and counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for imposing reciprocal discipline on a practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including what a respondent must file to contest, the effects of non-response, suspension terms, publication/notice obligations, and compliance and reinstatement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may request that the USPTO Director impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner based on a disciplinary order of a state court or bar, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order was entered pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) based on the June 2, 2009 order of the Supreme Court of New Jersey. Actions imposing reciprocal discipline cite applicable statutory/regulatory authority (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response requirement to contest imposition (40-day deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent seeks to contest imposition of suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the respondent must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information the respondent believes sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed Respondent that a timely filing within 40 days was required and specified that the response must contain all information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a response will permit the Director to determine there is no genuine issue and to impose discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to avoid identical discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent contesting reciprocal discipline must show a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the other jurisdiction would be unwarranted based on grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references the availability of grounds under § 11.24(d)(1) but does not enumerate them on the page; respondents must present factual/legal arguments within the 40-day response to raise such grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file the required response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and that suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not file a response to the Notice and Order; accordingly, the USPTO Director determined (1) no genuine issue existed under § 11.24(d) and (2) suspension from practice before the USPTO was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension terms and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may suspend a practitioner from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office for a specified period (here, six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly suspends Respondent from practice before the Office for a period of six (6) months (see ordering paragraph (a)). The scope covers patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may be granted limited recognition to practice for a short period (here, 30 days) beginning on the date of the Final Order to wind up client business and withdraw from employment in pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering paragraph (b) grants limited recognition beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days later; paragraph (c) directs the respondent to wind up client business and withdraw per § 10.40 during that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: During any limited recognition period to wind up matters, the practitioner is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering paragraph (d) explicitly directs Respondent not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish a notice of suspension in the Official Gazette describing the disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering paragraphs (e) and (f) require publication of the Final Order and an Official Gazette notice; disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the practitioner (name, registration number), state the period of suspension, cite the rule(s) violated, and summarize the basis for the discipline (including underlying state rule violations and conduct summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example notice includes: practitioner name and registration number; period of suspension (six months); violated USPTO rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)); the state rules violated (Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(b) and 8.4(c)); a factual summary of misconduct (e.g., collecting disability benefits while receiving income from consulting); statutory/regulatory basis for action (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59); and a link to the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligations during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: While suspended, the practitioner must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs Respondent to comply fully with § 11.58 while suspended (the page does not recite § 11.58's text but imposes the obligation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering paragraph (h) directs the OED Director to provide these notices in accordance with § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures and compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon any request for reinstatement, the practitioner shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering paragraph (i) directs Respondent to comply with § 11.60 on any reinstatement request; the Final Order does not enumerate § 11.60's specifics but imposes the statutory/regulatory reinstatement obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action before the USPTO is taken pursuant to federal statute and USPTO regulations (example here: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explicitly cites the statutory and regulatory provisions authorizing the disciplinary action; practitioners and OED should cite and follow the appropriate authorities when imposing or contesting discipline.
